fact: President Tinubu directed on 28 August 2026 a forensic audit of the Integrated Personnel and Payroll Information System, reviewing reported ghost workers and payroll fraud on the running system.
The audit directive of 28 August 2026 names GIFMIS, the Treasury Single Account and Sub-TSA as government platforms whose interfaces with IPPIS are to be examined.
The IPPIS Human Resource modules, covering payroll administration, serve over 508 federal MDAs and over 600,000 civil servants, per the Head of the Civil Service.
The IPPIS HR modules went live on 27 July 2026 on the locally developed SoftSuite platform, a migration from foreign software.
NITDA took over the Nigeria Government Enterprise Architecture infrastructure from KOICA at a handover in Abuja, reported 27 March 2026, with the NGEA described as now operational.
Federal MDAs remitted N1.96tn through IPPIS in 2024 per GovSpend data analysed by Punch; the OAGF site lists 308 MDAs fully on IPPIS.

The Accountant General of the Federation said on 16 June 2025 that salaries of federal tertiary institutions are now paid through GIFMIS after a transition from IPPIS, with delays and unremitted deductions reported.

The Accountant General said federal tertiary institutions' payroll moved from IPPIS to GIFMIS in an abrupt migration in the last quarter of 2024, after an October 2024 terminal date for IPPIS payroll operations.

The Office of the Accountant General of the Federation said on 22 October 2025 that IPPIS remains the Federal Government's central payroll platform for civil servants and that October salaries would be paid as scheduled.

The Office of the Accountant General of the Federation said one of IPPIS's payroll platforms was migrated to the SoftSuite application in 2024, with the remaining payroll consolidation onto SoftSuite under way in October 2025.

The Office of the Head of the Civil Service of the Federation reports the IPPIS Steering Committee met on 11 September 2025 to oversee the Integrated Personnel and Payroll Information System, the platform for federal personnel and payroll management.

Punch reports that the 2025 budget call circular requires every federal ministry, department and agency to be enrolled on IPPIS, which has processed salaries for over one million federal employees across 696 MDAs since 2007.

Punch reports that, under an Accountant-General circular of 8 October 2024, federal tertiary institutions' payroll payments would be made via the Government Integrated Financial Management Information System from November 2024.
